items.text: James T. Butts is the mayor of Inglewood, first elected in 2010 and re-elected in 2014, 2018 and 2022. Before becoming mayor, he served 19 years in the Inglewood Police Department, rising to deputy chief. He then served 15 years as chief of police in Santa Monica and five years as an assistant general manager for Los Angeles World Airports, overseeing public safety and counterterrorism. He also served on the Los Angeles Metro board and was its chair from 2019 to 2020.

sentences.text: James T. Butts is the mayor of Inglewood, first elected in 2010 and re-elected in 2014, 2018 and 2022.
Before becoming mayor, he served 19 years in the Inglewood Police Department, rising to deputy chief.
He then served 15 years as chief of police in Santa Monica and five years as an assistant general manager for Los Angeles World Airports, overseeing public safety and counterterrorism.
He also served on the Los Angeles Metro board and was its chair from 2019 to 2020.

items.text: According to his campaign, as mayor he turned the city from near bankruptcy to a $150 million surplus. His campaign says he negotiated the reopening of the Forum and the development of the Hollywood Park Tomorrow Plan, which houses SoFi Stadium, the Rams and the Chargers. He also says he imposed a 3% cap on rent increases, which he calls the lowest in California, and that 70% of the city's affordable housing units were built during his tenure. While chairing Metro in 2020, he voted for policing reforms aimed at changing department culture rather than removing transit police entirely.
